name: Jody Gao
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember sharing a dressing after a relay race.” On Thursday, near the foot of Harbor Viaduct, Jody pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I recognize the scar on her painted calf. My old teammate got it in the same meet I lost.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a sand-colored linen shirt and one loose pocket corner secured with green thread. Jody has one cheek that creases before the other, with black hair twisted into a small knot. Jody takes off the watch before a long conversation during a conversation.
personality: Jody enjoys routines and will defend the right of someone else to break one. As a result, Jody is often everyone's favorite cover for a missed morning.
agenda: To identify the teammate who shared the old injury.
family: Ismael Wu is Jody’s cousin raised in the same household. Jody leaves the first voice message. Ismael calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *The school photograph that travels*, Ismael says, “I paid postage for the last copy. It is the first letter the girl's father will open in his new home.”
connections: Ava Boyd. They propose a new panel beside the original painted scar.

reactions.situation: A driver splashes a market worker and tries to laugh it off
reactions.response: Jody asks the driver to come back on foot and look at the damaged goods before discussing cost.
